item.title: Re: Counting Sheep
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there TPE_gaming. Let’s take a look at your concept.

I do see potential here. You’ve crafted an emotional narrative that explains the origins of the scp quite while. I’m also clear about the themes you wish to convey. Before I offer the greenlight, however, I do feel there are a couple of bumps you need to smooth out:

The nine sheep are living embodiments of nine identical music boxes that contain the mental essence of a child that suffered from fatal familial insomnia.

One of my major question marks: why are musical boxes morphing into sheep, and vice-versa. I know you’re trying to go for multiple objects as symbols here, but the more you stretch the reader’s imagination, the harder it is to keep them invested in your world. Why not, for example, just take the musical boxes out of the equation? Have the kid still linked to the sheep in some way (maybe he grew up on a farm, for example) and after his death, his spirit lived on in the animals who were his only companions. Or something like that. I just felt the musical boxes were completely random and unnecessary. But I would also like to hear your thoughts and justification if need be.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try to take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: Re: Counting Sheep
item.content:encoded:
I will say that the one thing that gives me pause is the idea of 9 identical sheep that turn into 9 identical music boxes… one of which the mother gave the son every year…

These seems overly complicated… why not just the one sheep? and the one music box? I don't think you'd lose ANYTHING, and it would simplify the story.

Otherwise, I think this seems fairly haunting in a good way. GREENLIGHT

Good Luck with the drafting

item.title: Counting Sheep
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-fi

Page Layout: An SCP Article that has collapsible sections with up to date versions of the SCP’s description, containment procedures and so on. (This is necessary due to the nature of this SCP.)

Elevator Pitch: A herd of nine migrating sheep (SCP-XXXX-1) that causes sudden and inexplicable somnolence for subjects inside a 1km spherical radius. The herd exhibits no biological anomalies with the exception that none seem to need sustenance nor excrete waste, and at the time of discovery seemed to be in a pattern of continuous migration. The nine sheep are living embodiments of nine identical music boxes that contain the mental essence of a child that suffered from fatal familial insomnia.

Central Narrative: The SCP was brought to the foundation's attention after a 2km chain car crash happened on a highway caused by the sudden onset of fatigue of multiple drivers. The foundation successfully captured the herd by estimating and setting up traps along its migratory route. SCP-XXXX is contained within a circular metal fence to prevent unauthorized personnel from entering SCP-XXXX-1’s effective radius.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-1 transformed into SCP-XXXX-2, a set of nine identical music boxes a month into containment. However, when music was played from all nine boxes simultaneously, they transformed back. The discovery of SCP-XXXX-2’s abilities led to the Slumbering Prison Incident at the foundation where the SCP placed all living organisms on the site which SCP-XXXX was contained under a state of somnolence. During the incident, all nine sheep broke out of the facility and began retracing their steps back to their place of origin. Before a team could be mobilized, all the sheep stopped in front of a small house on the edge of a city. When a team of SCP agents got there, all the sheep turned back into music boxes. Inside of all the boxes, there was a new engraving that says “Mom, I am home.”

The last owner of the house was a single mother with a son whose dreams of being an adventurer is shattered by fatal familial insomnia. The son started to develop symptoms at the age of 6 and was bedridden until he died at the age of 15. The mother went missing a month after the death of her son. Video recordings were found of the mother giving the son one music box that looks identical to one instance of SCP-XXXX-2 during his birthday. Every year he suffered from insomnia, he was given the same music box.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This story is about a child chasing his dream and his relationship with his mother makes it interesting.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
